title: Lifestyle Diseases and Wellness
summary: Common lifestyle diseases (hypertension, type 2 diabetes, heart disease, cancer, obesity), risk factors, prevention and early detection, and the impact on individuals and South Africa.

notes.text: **Lifestyle diseases** (non-communicable diseases) are linked to the way people live: diet, activity, smoking, alcohol and stress. They are a leading cause of death in South Africa.

rows: Too much salt, obesity, stress, alcohol, inactivity
Less salt, exercise, healthy weight, regular check-ups
Obesity, sugary foods and drinks, inactivity, family history
Smoking, high cholesterol, hypertension, diabetes, inactivity
Not smoking, exercise, healthy fats, managing blood pressure
Smoking, alcohol, UV exposure, some infections (HPV)
Not smoking, sunscreen, HPV vaccine, screening

notes.label: Risk factors
notes.text: Some risk factors **cannot be changed** (age, genes, family history), but many **can** (diet, exercise, smoking, alcohol, stress). Changing these reduces risk significantly.

items: Regular blood pressure and blood sugar tests at clinics.
Breast self-examination and Pap smears (cervical cancer screening).

notes.title: Why screening helps
notes.problem: Why are blood pressure checks useful even if a person feels well?
steps: High blood pressure often has no symptoms.
Early treatment reduces the risk of stroke and heart disease.
notes.answer: It finds silent problems in time to treat them.

items: **Individual**: reduced quality of life, disability, early death, medical costs.
**Family**: loss of income, caring responsibilities, emotional strain.
**Country**: pressure on the health system, lost productivity, higher costs.

notes.title: Body Mass Index (BMI)
notes.problem: Calculate the BMI of a person with a mass of 78 kg and a height of 1,72 m.
notes.answer: About 26,4 (in the 'overweight' range of 25–29,9 for adults)

questions.prompt: Lifestyle diseases are also called non-… diseases. (one word)
Too much salt is a major risk factor for…
Which vaccine helps prevent cervical cancer?
Calculate the BMI of a person with mass 64 kg and height 1,60 m.
Family history is a risk factor that cannot be changed.
Match each disease to a major risk factor.
Suggest THREE lifestyle changes that reduce the risk of heart disease.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): stop smoking; exercise; healthy diet; less salt; maintain healthy weight; manage stress; limit alcohol

questions.prompt: Discuss the impact of lifestyle diseases on the South African economy.
questions.memo:
✓ Pressure on public health services and budgets (1)
✓ Lost productivity from illness and early death (1)
✓ Families lose income, increasing poverty (1)

questions.prompt: Why is early detection of diseases such as diabetes and hypertension important?
questions.memo:
✓ They often have no early symptoms (1)
✓ Early treatment prevents serious complications such as stroke, blindness or kidney failure (1)

questions.prompt: Why should young people care about lifestyle diseases now?
questions.memo:
✓ Habits formed young (diet, smoking, inactivity) continue into adulthood (1)
✓ Risk builds over time; prevention is easier than cure (1)
